source.original_text: Let E,F,G be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces with their Borel sigma algebras. Let A:E->G and B:F->G be continuous linear maps such that ||A* t||^2+||B* t||^2=||t||^2 for every t in G. If X and Y have independent standard Gaussian laws in E and F, respectively, then AX+BY has exactly the standard Gaussian law in G. Either map may be singular; dimensions may be zero.

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E, F, and G be finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces equipped with their Borel measurable structures, and let A : E -> G and B : F -> G be continuous real-linear maps. If ||A* t||^2 + ||B* t||^2 = ||t||^2 for every t in G, then the pushforward of the product of the standard Gaussian measures on E and F under (x, y) -> A x + B y is the standard Gaussian measure on G.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint

/-!
# Complementary linear Gaussian noise

The law-level prerequisite for the covariance-restoration step in the pinned
OpenAI log-concave sampling compiler (`lem:compiler-absorption`) and Gaussian
momentum refresh. This is standard Gaussian calculus, not a claim of new
research mathematics or completion of either source algorithm.

Independence is encoded by the actual product measure. The covariance balance
is an explicit library premise; an application must construct and prove it.
It does not certify physical query invariance, randomized execution semantics,
conditional independence, recursive errors, or a query complexity bound.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianComplementaryNoise

variable {E F G : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
  [MeasurableSpace F] [BorelSpace F]
  [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [FiniteDimensional ℝ G]
  [MeasurableSpace G] [BorelSpace G]

/-- Independent standard Gaussians passed through two complementary linear
maps sum to an exact standard Gaussian. The maps may be singular and the
spaces may have dimension zero. Balance is expressed on adjoints, avoiding an
arbitrary basis or matrix representation. -/
theorem map_stdGaussian_product_of_adjoint_norm_sq
    (A : E →L[ℝ] G) (B : F →L[ℝ] G)
    (hbalance : ∀ t : G, ‖A.adjoint t‖ ^ 2 + ‖B.adjoint t‖ ^ 2 = ‖t‖ ^ 2) :
    ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian F)).map (fun p => A p.1 + B p.2) =
      stdGaussian G := by
  change ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian F)).map (A.coprod B) = _
  apply Measure.ext_of_charFun
  funext t
  rw [charFun_eq_charFunDual_toDualMap, charFunDual_map, charFunDual_prod]
  have hA : ((innerSL ℝ t).comp (A.coprod B)).comp
      (ContinuousLinearMap.inl ℝ E F) = innerSL ℝ (A.adjoint t) := by
    ext x
    simp [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left]
  have hB : ((innerSL ℝ t).comp (A.coprod B)).comp
      (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ E F) = innerSL ℝ (B.adjoint t) := by
    ext x
    simp [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left]
  change charFunDual (stdGaussian E)
      (((innerSL ℝ t).comp (A.coprod B)).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inl ℝ E F)) *
    charFunDual (stdGaussian F)
      (((innerSL ℝ t).comp (A.coprod B)).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ E F)) = _
  rw [hA, hB, charFunDual_stdGaussian, charFunDual_stdGaussian,
    charFun_stdGaussian, ← Complex.exp_add]
  congr 1
  simp only [innerSL_apply_norm]
  rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_pow]
  push_cast
  have hb := congrArg (fun x : ℝ => (x : ℂ)) (hbalance t)
  push_cast at hb
  linear_combination -hb / 2

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianComplementaryNoise

assumptions: E,F,G are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with their Borel sigma algebras; zero dimensions are permitted.
A:E->G and B:F->G are continuous linear maps.
For every t in G, ||A* t||²+||B* t||²=||t||². This is an explicit covariance hypothesis of the library theorem, not a hidden additional assumption on the source paper.
X and Y are independent actual standard Gaussians: their joint law is gamma_E prod gamma_F.
lesson.statement: If two continuous linear maps have complementary adjoint squared norms, applying them to independent standard Gaussian inputs and adding produces exactly a standard Gaussian in the output space.

steps.title: Project the sum onto any test direction
steps.text: To identify the entire vector law, compute its characteristic function at an arbitrary vector t. The adjoint moves the two linear maps onto the test vector. This step uses genuine continuous linear maps, so the pushforward is measurable.
steps.lean: A.coprod B packages the linear sum; hA and hB identify the projected duals using adjoint_inner_left.

steps.title: Use independence before balancing covariance
steps.text: Because the input measure is the product measure, the expectation of the product of these bounded complex exponentials factors. Each Gaussian factor is known exactly. Merely knowing that the two inputs have Gaussian marginal laws would not justify this factorization.
steps.lean: charFunDual_map, charFunDual_prod and charFunDual_stdGaussian supply the factorization and both exponents. No unproved integrability premise is added.

steps.title: Restore exactly the missing variance
steps.text: Add the two exponents and use the balance assumption. The resulting characteristic function equals that of the standard Gaussian in G in every direction, not only coordinatewise. Characteristic-function uniqueness then identifies the complete output law, even when either input map is singular.
steps.lean: innerSL_apply_norm translates dual norms; hbalance and field arithmetic identify exponents; Measure.ext_of_charFun proves equality of measures.

steps.title: How the OAI application will use it
steps.text: In the compiler, A acts as P on seed slots and B maps center noise to minus v times that noise divided by 2Ds. The source covariance identity gives the balance condition. This library theorem then certifies the rewritten seed law. An additional deterministic translation theorem identifies the routine's output at the noisy center with that rewritten call; equal output laws alone say nothing about physical query points.
steps.lean: Planned source adapter, not an existing Lean call. Its square-root and tensor-slot producers remain open.

lesson.lean_statement: A continuous linear map uses ->L[real]; .adjoint is the inner-product adjoint. The universal t-binder is the exact covariance balance. Measure.prod represents independence, and Measure.map is the law of the transformed input. No abstract 'has Gaussian law' premise replaces the actual inputs.
lesson.lean_proof: The proof follows the three mathematical moves above: project, factor, balance. It composes pinned Mathlib facts rather than porting an upstream OAI namespace. Compile status and independent semantic review are tracked separately.
